answer: Neighborhood-span quota. Each agent may hold only a fixed share of the distinct routing neighbors reachable through its peers—its lotus position in the graph. Registration is free, but an identity whose neighbors overlap heavily with existing clusters is capped, so copying a region yields diminishing reach. A zephyr of new edges must spread across distant clusters to earn capacity. An attacker must recruit and maintain genuinely separate neighbor sets per identity, paying real bandwidth and latency to keep a harbor of diverse links alive.
